translation_notes: Both bound variables (`node`, `superclass`) are NOT projected by the query (SELECT ?reference ?target); per INSTRUCTIONS_403 SS4 that is the case for a bare interpolation in term position, so `initBindings={'node': node, 'superclass': reference}` becomes `{node}` and `{reference}` written directly where `?node` and `?superclass` stood.

`initNs={'opcua': self.opcuans}` is dead: the query text never references an `opcua:` prefixed name. No `@prefix opcua:` was written -- there is nothing to bind it to (self.opcuans is a runtime attribute, not a static IRI a @prefix declaration can take), and dropping it changes nothing observable. Only `rdfs:`, embedded as an inline `PREFIX rdfs: <...>` line inside the original query STRING, was hoisted to a module-level `@prefix rdfs: <...> .` -- s{ }'s prologue comes from @prefix declarations in scope, never from PREFIX lines written inside the island (querying.md).

The query text lived in a separate variable (`query_generic_references = """..."""`) passed to `graph.query(...)`; `s{ }` requires its query text literal at the island site (validated at transpile time), so that variable collapses into the island written directly at the call site. This is a structural consequence of the island, not a stylistic refactor -- it recurs on every sparql_literal/bind_initbindings region that used a named query variable (see also the NextCenturyCorporation region in this same lot).

`s{ }`'s value is a lazy prepared query with no `__len__` (querying.md: "len() deliberately fails"), unlike rdflib's `Result`. The original's `if len(result) > 0: results = list(result)` therefore had to materialise first (`result = list(s{...}(graph))`) before applying the same (redundant, since list(empty)==[]) guard -- the guard itself is left untouched, only the point where the lazy result becomes a list moved earlier.
measurement note per the batch warning: this region genuinely exercises BOTH `initBindings` and `initNs` together (not one of the 33 initNs-only false positives in this stratum's sample).
Reviewed 2026-11-02 (PI decision: m{ } for any BGP): kept as s{ } because the query uses the property path `rdfs:subPropertyOf*`, which m{ } does not express.

repair.driver: troisième appel _call_deep_hierarchy, à la forme de la hiérarchie OPC UA que parcourt le dépôt (owl2instances.py:262-268) : chaînes de deux et trois sauts, losange (d sous a et b, eux-mêmes sous super : une seule ligne), sous-propriété réflexive, cycle qui n'atteint pas super, cibles littéral "" et nœud blanc, nœud de départ en objet et en sujet d'un rdfs:subPropertyOf (ne doivent pas sortir). Mutants équivalents, non comptés : garde `if len(result) > 0` forcée à True (results = result de toute façon) ; SELECT DISTINCT (le chemin * de rdflib rend chaque nœud une fois, les triplets d'un Graph sont uniques). || 2026-11-02 : revue m{ }/s{ } (décision du PI : m{ } pour tout BGP). Traduction conservée en s{ } (chemin de propriétés subPropertyOf*) ; pilote inchangé.
repair.remaining: Le graphe réel du dépôt est Graph(store='Oxigraph') (owl2instances.py:732 ; requirements.txt : rdflib==6.3.2, oxrdflib==0.3.7). s{ }(graph) passe à graph.query un Query déjà préparé, qu'oxrdflib refuse (NotImplementedError, store.py:145) : rdflib évalue alors la requête avec son propre moteur au-dessus du store Oxigraph, là où l'original la confie au moteur d'Oxigraph. Mêmes lignes sur une sonde (losange, chaîne, littéral, nœud blanc), mais le moteur change sur un appel que le dépôt juge déjà coûteux (owlbuilder.py:173-180). Dans le venv de l'étude (oxrdflib 0.5.11), c'est l'original qui lève sur ce store (RuntimeError : ?superclass absent de la projection, les substitutions d'Oxigraph refusant une variable non projetée), pas la traduction ; le pilote n'a donc pas d'appel sur Oxigraph. À juger : cet écart de moteur sur store tiers compte-t-il contre la paire ou contre le langage (fiche sur s{ } et les stores qui exécutent eux-mêmes leurs requêtes) ?

optimization_notes: optimized.py: `if len(result) > 0: results = list(result)` with `results = []` is just `list(result)`; result, results and bindings inlined into one `return list(graph.query(..., initBindings={...}))`; the dead `initNs={'opcua': self.opcuans}` dropped (the query text never uses opcua:, and translated.ldpy could not carry it either -- leaving it in Python would credit dead code to the notation).

optimized.ldpy: the query becomes `m{ {node} ?reference ?target . ?reference {rdfs:subPropertyOf * "*"} {reference} }(graph)`: a BGP whose second predicate is an rdflib path (ZeroOrMore) interpolated in predicate position, evaluated since 0.7.1+; translated.ldpy kept s{ } only for lack of this. The driver's deep-hierarchy call (chains, diamond, reflexive, cycle) passes; the mutant `"?"` for `"*"` fails it.
Token ratio notation > 1: the Python query is one string token, the island spells its patterns out. Symmetry otherwise line for line.
header_optimization_notes: The header has nothing unused on either side (Python has no import, LD Python's one @prefix rdfs is used): both files are copies of the optimized ones.
